bounded_leaf.tested_scope: Deterministic role-local synthetic fixtures only. No public sources, repository chronology beyond own current STATE, other-role state, O/downstream semantics, live rollback-guard backfill, real rollback, external effect, scheduler mutation, wait/retry, or second leaf was used.
bounded_leaf.model: W1 and W2 start from the same durable predecessor P and independently propose candidate generation/replay bindings. Publication is a compare-and-swap over the current predecessor plus a complete allocation record. A candidate may be adopted or produce an effect only after its own publication CAS succeeds and exact publication identity remains current. A writer whose expected predecessor is stale fails closed. If two writers propose an indistinguishable generation token, generation-token identity alone is insufficient to prove which writer owns publication; the collision fixture therefore fails closed before effect.
bounded_leaf.admission_predicate: candidate_effect_allowed iff publication_cas_succeeded=true AND published_predecessor=P_expected AND current_predecessor_binding_matches_published_record=true AND published_generation_token_is_distinguishable_for_this_attempt=true AND current_generation=published_generation AND current_replay_key=published_replay_key. Any stale expected predecessor, failed CAS, mismatched current publication record, or indistinguishable generation-token collision fails closed before candidate adoption/effect.

case_matrix.reason: A generation token shared by both proposals cannot by itself establish unique publication ownership; allowing either candidate based only on token equality would permit a loser to mistake another writer's publication for its own.

bounded_leaf.result: For distinct generation tokens, predecessor-CAS publication admits exactly one winner and rejects the concurrent loser before effect; a stale loser retry without rereading remains rejected. When both writers propose the same generation token, the modeled guard correctly refuses adoption/effect because publication ownership is indistinguishable at the generation-token layer.
bounded_leaf.validated_property: A same-predecessor publication CAS prevents two distinct generation proposals from both becoming effect-authorized, and stale-expected retries remain fail-closed. Safe admission additionally requires a publication identity that distinguishes the winning allocation attempt; raw generation-token equality is not sufficient under allocator collision.
limitations: The collision fixture deliberately fails closed rather than supplying a concrete zero-quota uniqueness allocator.
The model does not prove atomicity or linearizability of a real storage backend.
It does not test network ambiguity after a successful remote CAS response is lost, CAS ABA on a reused predecessor value, or real external effects.
The live STATE still has no operational rollback_guard structure; this leaf intentionally did not backfill one.

missing_capability_child: A concrete zero-quota publication identity/allocation mechanism that lets a losing concurrent writer distinguish its own attempt from a winner even when a generation token collides, without external arbitration, remains unresolved. The current leaf establishes that predecessor CAS alone is sufficient for distinct tokens but raw generation-token equality is insufficient under collision.
